title: The Gram Panchayat of Vengaivasal
body: In 1997, the government of Tamil Nadu allotted two hectares of land to 71 government employees. The land fell within the area of the Gram Panchayat of Vengaivasal village. On instructions from higher authorities, the District Collector of Kancheepuram directed the President of the Gram Panchayat to pass a resolution endorsing the allotment. The President and the Gram Panchayat refused, and the Collector issued an order to acquire the land. The Gram Panchayat filed a writ petition in the Madras High Court. A single-judge bench upheld the Collector's order and ruled that the Panchayat's consent was not needed. The Panchayat appealed, and the Division Bench reversed that order, holding that the government order infringed the powers of the Panchayats and grossly violated their constitutional status. The village retained its land and its right to decide how to use it.

title: Funds of rural local bodies
body: A study of local government finances found that rural local bodies raise about 0.24 per cent of the total revenues collected by government in India, but they account for about 4 per cent of the total government expenditure. The Constitution lists 29 subjects that may be transferred to Panchayats, but many States have not transferred most of these subjects. Panchayats in such States mainly carry out welfare and development schemes designed by the State and central governments, and they depend on grants from these governments to do so. People at the local level have little say in choosing welfare programmes or in the allocation of resources.
